**Method 1**

When we multiply a complex number and its conjugate, the result is always the sum of squares of the real part and the imaginary part.

For the given complex number $z=-2+7\text{i},$ the real part is $\text{Re}(z)=-2,$ and the imaginary part is $\text{Im}(z)=7,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}z\overset{―}{z} & =(\text{Re}(z))^{2}+(\text{Im}(z))^{2} \\  & =(-2)^{2}+{7}^{2} \\  & =4+49 \\  & =53.\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

Alternatively, we can actually carry out the process of multiplying the complex number and its conjugate.

To obtain the conjugate of the complex number $z=-2+7\text{i},$ we flip the sign of the imaginary part and get $\overset{―}{z}=-2-7\text{i}.$

Multiplying, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}z\overset{―}{z} & =(-2+7\text{i})(-2-7\text{i}) \\  & =(-2)^{2}+(-2)(-7)\text{i}+(7)(-2)\text{i}-{\text{i}}^{2}(7)^{2} \\  & =4+\cancel{14\text{i}}-\cancel{14\text{i}}-(-1)(49) \\  & =4+49 \\  & =53.\end{aligned}
$$
